title: Guard: re-check member manifests when root workspace renames change
description:
When the guard checks a proposed edit to the root Cargo.toml that changes [workspace.dependencies] renames, it currently only checks the root manifest itself against the new rename map. Member manifests that use `workspace = true` aliases are not re-checked — so adding `innocent = { package = "arrow-core" }` to the root passes the guard even if a member already has `innocent = { workspace = true }` and arrow-core is constrained.

The guard needs to detect when a root manifest edit changes the rename map, then scan and re-check all member manifests that reference the affected aliases.

Found by Codex adversarial review of sutra/148, partially addressed in ddc0352 (root manifest uses proposed content for its own rename map).

acceptance_criteria.text: Editing root Cargo.toml to add/change a workspace dep rename is blocked by the guard when a member manifest already uses that alias with workspace=true and the real package is constrained
No performance regression for root Cargo.toml edits that don't touch workspace renames
Waiver handling works per-member (waivers on server/Cargo.toml apply to server findings)

implementation_plan:
When check_manifest_raw checks the root Cargo.toml:
1. Build proposed rename map from content (already done after ddc0352)
2. Build current rename map from on-disk root manifest
3. Diff the two maps — if no new/changed renames, stop (zero overhead for normal edits)
4. For each affected alias, scan member manifests via scan_workspace_manifests, find any with `alias = { workspace = true }`
5. Re-check those members with the proposed rename map via check_manifest + waiver partition
6. Merge findings into result

Extract a helper `check_manifest_with_waivers` that takes (conn, constraints, manifest_rel_path, content, renames) and does check_manifest + waiver partition → CheckOutcome. Avoids recursion and keeps waiver handling correct per-manifest.

check_manifest_raw becomes:
- Root path: build proposed renames from content, call helper for root, diff renames, call helper for each affected member
- Member path: read root from disk, call helper

Edge cases: alias removed (Cargo build error, not our problem), alias changed (diff catches), multiple aliases (all handled in one scan), member also being edited in same session (guard fires per-file, ordering is correct for pre-write hooks).

Cost: member scan only runs when rename map changes (rare). <50 member crates = <1ms IO.

messages.author: codex
messages.text:
Codex adversarial review: **needs-attention**

Two findings:

1. **[high] Root rename edits can be blocked by unrelated pre-existing member violations** (check.rs:759-772) — The member recheck appends ALL active findings from scanned members, not just findings introduced by the rename change. A root edit changing alias B can be denied because a member has an unrelated pre-existing forbidden dependency. Fix: diff old_renames vs proposed findings, only surface newly introduced ones.

2. **[medium] Member recheck scans non-workspace Cargo.toml files** (external.rs:383-417) — scan_workspace_manifests walks the filesystem for all Cargo.toml files, not just declared workspace members. Vendored crates, examples, or nested independent workspaces get evaluated with the top-level rename map and can falsely block. Fix: drive recheck from proposed [workspace].members expansion.

Next steps: Add regression tests for both cases; change recheck to diff old-vs-proposed findings and restrict scan to actual workspace members.
